title: Dowman at the North London derby v Henry and Fàbregas at the same age
checked: Tottenham v Arsenal 6 Dec 2026 (both clubs' 2026-27 season pages). Dowman born 31 Dec 2009 = 16 years 340 days that day. Youngest PL scorer 16y73d v Everton 14 Mar 2026 (Premier League + Sky + Wikipedia); youngest PL starter 16y144d, 24 May 2026 (AP via WTOP + Wikipedia); Arsenal 2025-26 champions (Sofascore + OFM); 8 league games, 1 league goal to 27 Oct 2026 (Wikipedia, so 'at least'). Fàbregas at the same age (8 Apr 2004): debut 28 Oct 2003 aged 16y177d, youngest scorer 16y212d v Wolves, no league games yet (Arsenal.com + Football Faithful). Henry at the same age (23 Jul 1994): no first-team games; debut 31 Aug 1994 v Nice at 17 (Wikipedia + 90min); 1994-95: 8 league games, 3 goals (Wikipedia only). Minutes not confirmable, so the twist uses games.

lines.text: When Arsenal go to Tottenham on the sixth of December, Max Dowman will be sixteen years and three hundred and forty days old.
He's already the youngest scorer in Premier League history. Sixteen years and seventy-three days, against Everton.
Then the youngest player to start a Premier League game. And a title winner, as Arsenal won the league.
So what had Arsenal's legends done at exactly the same age?
Cesc Fàbregas, April twenty oh-four. He'd become Arsenal's youngest ever player and scorer, but in the League Cup.
Premier League games at that age? Zero.
Thierry Henry, July nineteen ninety-four. He hadn't even made his debut for Monaco. That came a month later, at seventeen.
So at this age, Dowman has played at least eight league games. Henry and Fàbregas, none.
Now the twist. Match the games. In Henry's first eight league games, he scored three times. Dowman has one.
And Henry went on to score one hundred and seventy-five league goals for Arsenal. A club record.
So does Dowman become the next Henry, the next Cesc, or something bigger? Tell me in the comments.
